title: Story 1 — Embed Dagger into the app SQLite database
description: Refactor Dagger storage so it can run against a caller-provided SQLite pool in addition to a standalone path. This lets RZN host Dagger inside the main app database instead of maintaining a separate demo-style `tasks.db`.
acceptance_criteria:
- Add a pool-based storage constructor alongside the path-based constructor.
- The pool-based constructor initializes Dagger tables idempotently.
- Dagger can still be used in standalone mode for tests and examples.
- Documentation explains when to use pool-based vs path-based initialization.
close_reason: Implemented embedded durable task plane v1: namespaced dagger_* schema, public metadata, host queries, stop/soft-delete semantics, and recovery/migration coverage.

title: Dagger Durable Task Plane v1 — Embedded Storage, Public Metadata, and Host Queries
close_reason: Implemented embedded durable task plane v1: namespaced dagger_* schema, public metadata, host queries, stop/soft-delete semantics, and recovery/migration coverage.

title: Story 3 — Add public task metadata for host integration
description: Extend the Dagger task model with the public metadata RZN needs to project provider-facing durable tasks, including thread binding, subject, description, owner, source metadata, and arbitrary metadata JSON.
acceptance_criteria:
- The task model stores `public_id`, `thread_id`, `subject`, `description`, `owner`, and metadata JSON explicitly.
- Source metadata can record originating surface, tool name, thread, turn, run, and call identifiers.
- The storage layer round-trips the public metadata losslessly.
- Documentation explains the distinction between engine/runtime fields and host/public fields.
close_reason: Implemented embedded durable task plane v1: namespaced dagger_* schema, public metadata, host queries, stop/soft-delete semantics, and recovery/migration coverage.

title: Align embedded dagger schema with host migration
description: Adopt the canonical dagger_* table layout used by the RZN app migration so Dagger no longer creates or queries a divergent schema when embedded into a host SQLite database.
close_reason: Aligned embedded dagger_* schema and migration paths with the host SQLite contract; added regression coverage for fresh schema shape and old embedded-schema upgrades.

title: Dagger: Lobster-like primitives for RZN Work Queue execution
description: Enable deterministic batch execution for Outbox/Work Queue items (approve selected → stage/send), plus a reusable exec/pipeline primitive with enterprise-grade audit + guardrails.
design: Context: RZN desktop app is adding a global Work Queue view with batch containers (expand to items) and multi-select approve/reject/send/retry. Execution should be one run per user action, with per-item isolation for retries and strong audit. OpenClaw's cron/heartbeat + Lobster patterns are reference points (needs_approval + resume token, deterministic pipelines).
close_reason: Completed Work Queue primitives: exec (system/sidecar + caps), batch fanout helper w/ deterministic ids, pipeline compiler with text/json piping, runtime events fixes + domain events, HITL checkpoints/resume tokens, and docs/examples.

title: Batch execution helper: fanout selected items into per-item steps
description: Provide a first-class pattern/helper to execute a user-selected subset of items (e.g., Outbox batch) as one run, while keeping per-item isolation for retries and audit.
design: RZN Work Queue will present one container WorkItem with expand→items. Users multi-select items and click Approve/Reject/Send/Retry. Execution should be a single Dagger run per click, but each item should map to a stable step/branch so partial failures don't block the rest and retries can target only failed items.
acceptance_criteria:
- Given inputs {container_id, selected_item_ids[], approved_revision_ids[]}, build/execute a DAG that runs one sub-step per selected item (parallel where possible).
- One item failing must not stop unrelated items (configurable continue-on-error).
- Execution report exposes an item_id → step_id (and/or branch_id) mapping for host audit/UI.
- Support retrying only failed items without re-running succeeded ones (via cache keys or explicit skip nodes).
- Deterministic step_id naming to support idempotency + clean event timelines.
close_reason: Implemented batch fanout helper + deterministic per-item step IDs + continue-on-error; added example + tests.

title: Exec primitive: structured command spec + caps (system/sidecar)
description: Add a reusable Lobster-like exec capability: one structured exec action/tool that runs an executable with args and returns structured outputs with strict resource caps.
design: Goal is to avoid 'arbitrary shell' while still enabling powerful workflows. Spec should support kind=sidecar (bundled/managed) vs kind=system (allowlisted), with policy enforced by host. Output caps/timeouts must be enforced centrally.
acceptance_criteria:
- Define a stable ExecSpec { kind, executable, args[], cwd, env, stdin, timeout_ms, max_stdout_bytes, max_stderr_bytes, parse_stdout_as_json } and ExecResult { exit_code, stdout, stderr, stdout_json?, truncated, duration_ms }.
- No shell interpolation by default (no 'sh -c'); args[] are passed directly.
- Enforce timeouts and output caps; mark truncation explicitly.
- Support JSON piping patterns (stdout_json) for downstream nodes.
- Provide clear host extension points for sidecar resolution + allowlists + approval gating (do not bake RZN-specific policy into dagger core).
- Add at least one example workflow demonstrating JSON-in/JSON-out exec.
close_reason: Implemented ExecSpec/ExecResult + host policy hooks + caps/timeout enforcement; added exec action + example + tests.

title: Pipeline compiler: steps + pipes → DAG nodes (no sh -c)
description: Provide a helper that turns a Lobster-style 'pipeline spec' (steps with stdin/stdout wiring) into Dagger DAG nodes with explicit dependencies.
design: This is the ergonomics layer: users specify steps; dagger generates node graph. Prefer deterministic wiring (prev.stdout or prev.stdout_json to next.stdin) and allow parallelism where no dependency exists.
acceptance_criteria:
- Accept a pipeline spec (array of steps) and emit NodeSpecs + dependencies for a DAG.
- Support piping modes: raw text (stdout→stdin) and JSON (stdout_json→next inputs).
- Avoid opaque shell pipelines; each step is its own exec node.
- Preserve step ordering deterministically; allow explicit fanout when specified.
- Document how the generated node IDs relate to step indices for audit and retries.
close_reason: Implemented work_queue pipeline compiler (PipelineSpec → Graph) with text/json piping, deterministic step ids, exec.stdin_json support, tests, and documented contract.

title: HITL checkpoints: pause/resume contract with resume tokens
description: Standardize a Lobster-like 'needs_approval' outcome for workflows so host apps can pause a branch, collect human input/approval, then resume deterministically.
design: OpenClaw Lobster returns needs_approval + resumeToken; you resume with a token + approve flag. In RZN, interactive tool execution already uses pause/resume; we want a reusable Dagger-native pattern for any node/action to request human approval without bespoke glue.
acceptance_criteria:
- Define a canonical way for an action/hook to signal 'needs approval' with a structured payload (prompt + editable schema/payload reference).
- Pause the appropriate branch before side effects occur.
- Provide a stable resume token shape sufficient to resume the run/branch/node after approval (without re-running earlier steps).
- Ensure the paused state + reason is observable via runtime events (BranchStateUpdated or equivalent).
- Document the expected host responsibilities (persist approval objects, render UI, call resume).
close_reason: Implemented HITL checkpoints via hitl_checkpoint action + HitlRuntime resume tokens, branch pause/resume runtime events + domain events, ServiceRegistry for multi-service embedding, tests, and contract docs.

title: Runtime events: fix run_id/branch_id semantics + allow domain events
description: Tighten runtime event semantics for pause/resume and enable emitting domain-specific events needed for enterprise audit.
design: Today BranchStateUpdated emission sets envelope.run_id=branch_id in dag_flow pause/resume code (src/dag_flow/dag_flow.rs). For host apps (RZN), run_id and branch_id are distinct. Also, Work Queue and automation flows will benefit from a way to emit audited domain events (e.g., work_item.state_changed) without abusing ToolInvoked.
acceptance_criteria:
- BranchStateUpdated events include the actual flow run_id in the envelope, and branch_id remains a field on the event.
- Ensure step_id and branch_id naming guidance is documented for host apps.
- Provide a minimal, typed way to emit custom/domain events with JSON payload (or a constrained StatusUpdate/MetricRecorded style event) without breaking existing reducers.
- Add/adjust docs describing how host apps should consume these events for UI timelines.
close_reason: Fixed BranchStateUpdated envelope.run_id semantics; added DomainEvent runtime event + DagExecutor::emit_domain_event; updated docs.

title: Docs + examples: batch outbox send + partial failure + retry
description: Write a concrete example workflow + narrative showing how to execute a selected subset of items as one run with per-item isolation, then retry failures.
design: This is the handoff artifact for the RZN hooks/skills teams. It should demonstrate the intended Dagger API usage (fanout helper, exec primitive, event sink, pause/resume if relevant) and show how host integrates approval staging vs approve+send.
acceptance_criteria:
- Add an example (code + sample YAML/spec) that runs N items, continues on error, and produces a structured report.
- Show how to retry only failed items.
- Show where approvals fit (stage vs approve+send) without requiring host-specific UI.
- Keep the example deterministic and auditable (stable IDs, clear logs/events).
close_reason: Added worked example + YAML spec for batch send with partial failure and retry-only-failed; documented flow and where approvals/HITL fit; updated docs and examples index.

title: Gate 0 — Dagger↔Host contract (ExecSpec, batch fanout, events, resume tokens)
description: Define the Dagger-side contract for RZN integration: batch execution helper shape, ExecSpec/ExecResult, runtime events semantics (run_id vs branch_id), and pause/resume tokens.
acceptance_criteria:
- ExecSpec/ExecResult defined and documented.
- Batch fanout helper inputs/outputs defined (item_id→step_id mapping).
- Runtime events semantics corrected/documented.
- Pause/resume token contract documented (host responsibilities).
close_reason: Documented Dagger↔Host Work Queue contract (exec/batch/events/HITL resume token) in docs/WORK_QUEUE_CONTRACT.md and linked from docs/README.md.

title: Story 6 — Add recovery and migration coverage for embedded durable tasks
description: Prove that the refactored Dagger storage survives restart, recovery, and schema migration without corrupting task state.
acceptance_criteria:
- Tests cover recovery of accepted/running tasks after restart.
- Tests cover dependency reconstruction from the relational edge table.
- Tests cover output/event history persistence across restart.
- Tests cover migration or fresh initialization into the embedded `dagger_*` schema.
close_reason: Implemented embedded durable task plane v1: namespaced dagger_* schema, public metadata, host queries, stop/soft-delete semantics, and recovery/migration coverage.

description: Expose query methods that let the app treat Dagger as a durable task repository instead of an execution-only store.
acceptance_criteria:
- Add storage queries for get-by-public-id, list-by-thread, list-children, list-dependencies, and list-dependents.
- Add append/list APIs for ordered task outputs.
- Add append/list APIs for task lifecycle events.
- Query performance is supported by indexes on thread, status, parent, and dependency edges.
close_reason: Implemented embedded durable task plane v1: namespaced dagger_* schema, public metadata, host queries, stop/soft-delete semantics, and recovery/migration coverage.

title: Story 5 — Formalize status mapping, stop semantics, and soft deletion
description: Make Dagger statuses and task lifecycle transitions explicit enough for provider-facing task CRUD adapters, including stop/cancel behavior and soft deletion/tombstones.
acceptance_criteria:
- Dagger documents the mapping between engine statuses and host/public statuses.
- Stop/cancel semantics are implemented consistently and persisted.
- Soft delete or tombstone semantics exist without losing task history.
- Status reason and output summary can be surfaced cleanly to the host.
close_reason: Implemented embedded durable task plane v1: namespaced dagger_* schema, public metadata, host queries, stop/soft-delete semantics, and recovery/migration coverage.

title: Story 2 — Replace the legacy task schema with embedded `dagger_*` tables
description: Move Dagger off the current generic `tasks` and `shared_state` tables and onto an embedded, namespaced schema with tables for jobs, tasks, dependencies, outputs, events, and shared state.
acceptance_criteria:
- Introduce `dagger_jobs`, `dagger_tasks`, `dagger_task_dependencies`, `dagger_task_outputs`, `dagger_task_events`, and `dagger_shared_state`.
- Dependencies are stored relationally instead of only as serialized JSON arrays.
- Jobs and tasks have stable primary keys and public ids.
- Updated storage initialization is idempotent and migration-safe.
- Existing recovery and scheduler logic work with the new schema.
close_reason: Implemented embedded durable task plane v1: namespaced dagger_* schema, public metadata, host queries, stop/soft-delete semantics, and recovery/migration coverage.
